title: How this page works
subtitle: The three steps, drawn by the renderer they describe
description: The landing page explains itself in its own notation. This document is rendered by the same engine, from the same format, as every other page in this file — so the hero is not a picture of the product, it is the product running.

workflows.title: Turn a process into a page you can send
workflows.description: Three steps. You run the middle one — this page never sees your process until you paste the finished workflow back in, and it does not read it then either.

summary.trigger: A process exists in someone's head
summary.outcome: One self-contained HTML file you can send to anyone

start.label: A process exists, undrawn
start.note: In someone's head, or in a flowchart nobody reads

detail.purpose: The prompt and the renderer both travel inside this page. Copying the prompt fetches nothing and tells no one you did it.
procedure: Open the builder and press Copy on the prompt.
Nothing leaves your machine at this step.

steps.title: Paste it into your own model, with your process
steps.note: You run this step, not this page

detail.purpose: This is the only step where your process text leaves your machine, and it goes to the model vendor you already chose — on their terms, not ours. This page is not involved and never sees it.
procedure: Start a fresh conversation; the prompt is long and does badly with prior context.
Paste the prompt, then describe your process underneath it.
The reply should be one fenced JSON block and nothing else.

failureModes.when: The reply is wrapped in explanation
failureModes.then: Keep only what is between the fences

steps.title: Render it here, or run the renderer yourself?

detail.purpose: Nothing here is a service, so there is nothing to be locked into. The renderer that draws this page is the same code you can run locally, and the format is a plain JSON file. If you would rather your workflow never touched someone else's page at all, this is the supported path, not a workaround.
procedure: Clone the repository and run ./build.sh — Node, no package install.
Or open the downloaded index.html and use the builder inside it offline.
The document format is the same either way, so a file built here opens there.

detail.purpose: The build is deterministic: the same document produces the same page every time, here or on your machine. That is what makes the two paths genuinely interchangeable rather than a hosted version and a lesser one.

commands.note: Tests, builds, and proves the file stands alone

exit.label: Same file, built on your own machine

detail.purpose: This page will render your workflow without ever reading it — but you do not have to take that on trust. The renderer is open source, so the whole thing runs on your machine with nothing pasted anywhere.
rules: Both paths use the same renderer and produce the same file.
Neither path sends your document anywhere.

steps.title: Paste the workflow back here
steps.note: The renderer draws it without reading it

detail.purpose: The renderer is mechanical: it validates the shape of the document and lays out what it finds. It makes no judgement about your process and sends nothing anywhere.
rules: The first character must be { and the last must be }.
Same document in, same page out, every time.

branches.label: No
branches.note: The validator names the path and the rule

steps.title: Send the validator output back to the model

detail.purpose: The validator's message is written to be pasted straight back. It names the path that failed and the rule it broke, which is usually all the model needs to return a corrected document.
procedure: Copy the whole error, including the JSON path.
Take the corrected document whole; do not merge it by hand.

detail.purpose: The only gate. It checks that the document is the right shape, not that your process is any good — that judgement stays with you and the people who run it.

steps.title: Download one HTML file
steps.note: No server, no build, no dependencies

detail.purpose: What comes out is a single file that carries its own renderer, styles and content. It opens from a mail attachment on a laptop with no network.
procedure: Send it, commit it next to the code it describes, or host it anywhere.
Or download the renderer instead and run the whole thing yourself.

end.label: A page you can send
end.note: One file, every box worth opening
